Title: AKU and Nova Medical School partnership bears fruit
NewsSummary: 21 healthcare practitioners graduate from a specialized training programme

content.text: Twenty-one doctors from NOVA Medical School, medical specialists, residents and interns, graduated from a Clinical Investigator Training Programme (CITP) conducted by the Aga Khan University. CITP is designed to train healthcare practitioners to be clinical investigators and improve quality of research in institutions.

The three-month programme was a blend of face-to-face and online sessions that covered ethics of clinical trials, good clinical practice, development and writing of clinical protocols, budget for clinical trials and statistical concepts applied to clinical research.

"We are very pleased to have organized this clinical research course, with our partners from the Aga Khan University, with whom we are always very eager and excited to collaborate," said Helena Canhão, Dean at Nova Medical School. "This was a great opportunity for us, the faculty of NOVA Medical School, to be together, to think, to learn, to empower ourselves, by sharing knowledge, best practices and experience with the members of the Aga Khan University. All of us at NMS are enthusiastic to continue collaborating with AKU to advance knowledge and training teaches in the best tools for a clinical practice combined to research".

Professor Mansoor Saleh, founding director of AKU's Clinical Research Unit led the training and shared best practices and his vast experience in the field. In 2021, Prof Mansoor led the programme at AKU in Nairobi. Two cohorts of 40 participants completed the course and are now equipped to begin investigator-led trials or pharmaceutical sponsor clinical trials.

Following the success of this training, AKU partnered with Nova Medical School in Lisbon to offer CITP to professors, medical specialists and residents. This partnership has opened doors of opportunity for collaboration in research and healthcare.

"CITP is one example of how a committed academic partnership can result in a tangible outcome that can positively impact the career path of a clinician.  CITP is indeed that epigenetic stimulus that can awaken the "clinical research gene" in clinicians," said Dr Carl Amrhein, Provost and Vice President, Academic at AKU.
Participants had this to say about the training:

Fátima Serrano, professor and researcher at NOVA Medical School said, "Participating in the CITP training was very enriching. It challenges the participants by making us pause from our work routine and pushes us to transcend the boundaries of our current abilities. Moreover, through this training, I had the opportunity to meet exceptional colleagues, including some from my own institution that I did not know before, which will enable me to create synergies in the future."

"In order to conduct highest level clinical research now and in the future, and to promote the use of its results into clinical practice, I consider my enrollment into the CITP one of the best educational opportunities I could pursued," said Ana Rita Maria, Invited Assistant and PhD candidate at NOVA Medical School.
AKU hopes to implement CITP at all University and Aga Khan Health Services sites. This will in turn improve clinical research and empower clinicians become leaders in this field.
